rationale: Water damage from the policyholder's own burst plumbing to their home's basement structure and contents is direct property damage covered under homeowners insurance.
claim_summary: Homeowner Sam Patel returned from a work trip to find approximately two inches of water throughout the basement caused by a burst plumbing supply line. Damage includes buckled hardwood flooring, drywall saturation up to one foot, and ruined stored boxes. Estimated damage is $15k–$35k and requires urgent assessment for structural impact and mold prevention.

case_facts.description: two inches of water across entire basement, hardwood floor buckled, drywall soaked up to one foot, stored boxes ruined
case_facts.estimated_damage: water damage across entire basement including hardwood flooring, drywall, and contents — likely $15,000–$35,000 range pending assessment

rationale: Wind damage to roof shingles on the policyholder's own home is classic property damage coverage.
claim_summary: Jordan Lee's policy POL-1006 covers wind damage to four roof shingles above the back porch, estimated at $400 in repairs with no interior damage. However, the $2,500 deductible exceeds the estimated damage, meaning no benefit will be payable under the policy.

case_facts.description: four shingles blown off by wind, no interior damage
